slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: At neutral pH, calcium forms a blue complex with arsenazo III; the colour intensity is proportional to the calcium concentration.
About 99% of body calcium is in bone; a fall in albumin lowers serum calcium.
Low calcium: hypoparathyroidism, vitamin D deficiency, malabsorption; high: cancers, large vitamin D intake, hyperparathyroidism and others.

This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “Calcium-A III” kit (IFU BSIS09-I, 07/11/22). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: serum or plasma separated from the cells quickly. Oxalate or EDTA plasma is not acceptable — they chelate calcium. Stable 10 days at 2–8 °C.
24-hour urine: collect into calcium-free containers holding 10 mL of diluted nitric acid (50% v/v); record the volume; dilute 1/2 and multiply the result by 2.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Reagent: imidazole buffer pH 6.5 100 mmol/L, arsenazo III. Standard: calcium 10 mg/dL (aqueous primary).
Equipment: spectrophotometer or analyser reading at 650 nm, 1.0 cm cuvettes; disposable ware is recommended.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: The reagent and standard are ready to use.
Store the kit at 2–8 °C protected from light. Signs of deterioration: particles, turbidity or blank absorbance at 650 nm ≥ 0.50.
If glassware is used, clean it with diluted (1/2) HNO3 and rinse well with distilled water; chelating agents in detergents invalidate the result.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.
The values come from the SPINREACT “Calcium-A III” IFU (BSIS09-I). The IFU of the kit you use and the analyser manual always take precedence — check the programme against them.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 1. Conditions: wavelength 650 nm; temperature 37 °C or 15–25 °C.
2. Use a 1 cm cuvette; zero the instrument with distilled water.
3. Pipette into a cuvette: blank — reagent 1.0 mL; standard — reagent 1.0 mL + standard 10 µL; sample — reagent 1.0 mL + sample 10 µL.
4. Mix and incubate: 2 min at 37 °C or 15–25 °C.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 5. Read the absorbance (A) of the sample and standard against the blank; the colour is stable for at least 1 hour.

slides.title: Semi-automatic analyser: calcium programme
rows: Sample and standard — against the reagent blank

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: Result (mg/dL) = (A sample − A blank) / (A standard − A blank) × 10 (standard concentration).
24-hour urine: result × urine volume (dL/24 h) = mg/24 h. Conversion: mg/dL × 0.25 = mmol/L.
Linear up to 32 mg/dL; above that, dilute the sample 1/2 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 2.

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: IFU reference: adults 8.5–10.5 mg/dL (2.1–2.6 mmol/L), children 10–12 mg/dL, newborns 8–13 mg/dL; urine (adults) 50–300 mg/24 h.
These values are for orientation; each laboratory should establish its own reference range.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Triglycerides up to 1.25 g/L do not interfere.
Oxalate and EDTA chelate calcium — plasma from such tubes gives falsely low results.
Poorly rinsed glassware (chelating agents in detergents) invalidates the result.
IFU: calibration with the aqueous standard may cause a systematic error in automatic procedures — a serum calibrator is then recommended.
Drugs and other interfering substances are listed in the literature (IFU — Young DS).

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Assayed control sera are run with each series (IFU: SPINTROL H Normal and Pathologic).
If a control falls outside its range, check the instrument, reagents and calibrator; do not release patient results.
Each laboratory sets its own quality-control scheme and the corrective actions when controls are out of tolerance.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Reagent: H360 — may damage fertility or the unborn child; H371 — may cause damage to organs; contains methanol. Read the SDS.
Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
Used cuvettes, tubes and tips are disinfected.
